description: A pure CALCULATION node — row-wise vector maths on an N×2 list: Normalize, Length, Perpendicular, Negate, Angle. An N×2 matrix IS a list of N 2D vectors, so this reuses the matrix type. Draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: a LIST OF VECTORS in, a list out. Every row is treated as one vector and handled independently, so a whole polygon's worth of edges is processed in one pass — no Loop needed. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

THE TYPE: an N×2 matrix and a list of N 2D vectors are the same thing, so this node consumes anything the Matrix nodes produce — including a point list (`val-points`) or an edge-vector list (Shift Rows → Matrix Operations Subtract). A single vector is just the N = 1 case. N×3 works too where the operation is defined in 3D.

OPERATIONS:
• Normalize (v̂) — unit length, direction only. A zero-length row stays zero instead of becoming NaN.
• Length (|v|) — reduces to an N×1 column. Feed it back in as a per-row scalar via Matrix Operations (broadcasting).
• Perpendicular (CCW) — rotate 90°, (x, y) → (−y, x). For a COUNTER-CLOCKWISE ring this is the INWARD edge normal, which is what offsetting needs. 2D only (reads the first two columns).
• Perpendicular (CW) — (x, y) → (y, −x); the outward normal for a CCW ring.
• Negate (−v) — reverse direction.
• Angle — atan2(y, x) in DEGREES, reduces to an N×1 column.

OUTPUT: `val-matrix` plus `val-rows` / `val-cols`. Chain with Vector Product (dot / cross) and Matrix Operations to build geometric formulas directly in the graph. Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
